reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports all key premises: it shows serrated boundaries improve creep life and ductility, explains the mechanism via strain distribution and reduced intergranular cracking, and demonstrates that slower cooling induces serration. However, the evidence is from a bulk SLM HEA with post heat treatment, not from laser-cladded multilayer coatings, so the direct applicability to the proposed processing route is assumed rather than demonstrated.
premises: Serrated grain boundaries in HEAs increase tensile fracture strain and creep rupture life
Serrated boundaries distribute strains more evenly than straight boundaries
Serrated boundaries reduce strain concentration at triple junctions and intergranular cracking
Reduced cooling rate (via heat treatment) can induce serrated grain boundaries in HEAs
The mechanism is effective at elevated temperatures (e.g., 650°C)
